registerNote: GF(2) linear algebra. These are the PARAMETERS a stabilizer code would have. No claim that a physical quantum state exists in Zeta.
convention: CSS(C,C) for C^perp subset C yields [[n, 2*dim(C) - n, d]] with d = min weight over C \ C^perp.

adinkra_8_4_4.note: The committed AdinkraCode.generator: extended Hamming [8,4,4], doubly-even AND self-dual.

steane_punctured_7_4_3.note: AdinkraCode punctured at coordinate 0. Weight 3 and 7 are ODD: this code has LEFT the adinkra category.

rm_1_4.note: Reed-Muller RM(1,4): doubly-even, self-orthogonal, NOT self-dual. A bona fide adinkra code at N=16.

adinkra_8_0_4.note: k=0 IDENTICALLY: self-duality forces dim C = n/2. A stabilizer STATE, encoding nothing.

steane_7_1_3.note: Steane. Provenance from our own matrix by one puncture -- NOT inheritance; the puncture destroys doubly-evenness.

quantum_rm_16_6_4.note: Quantum Reed-Muller [[16,6,4]] (Calderbank-Shor 1996, Steane 1996). Defining code RM(1,4) stays INSIDE the adinkra category.

n8AdinkraClosure.domain: CSS(C^perp, C^perp) for C a doubly-even binary code of length 8 -- the adinkra category. NOT all 8-qubit stabilizer codes: [[8,3,3]] (Calderbank-Rains-Shor-Sloane 1997) beats every row but does not split into X and Z parts, so it comes from no binary code. Cited, not computed.
n8AdinkraClosure.result: No code in this domain both encodes a qubit and corrects an error: d=4 with k=0, or k>0 with d<=2.
